turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Howzit, come sit, the doctor's just wrapping up next door.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, sorry I'm late hey. That robot by the mall was out and I sat there forever.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Ah, don't worry about it. My sister's little one had a fever last week and she was late for everything, sat at the clinic with him the whole morning.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yoh. Poor kid. Anyway, I'm here.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello. Come through. You look like you'd rather be somewhere else.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ha. My wife made the booking. I'm forty-four, I'm fine, really. It's nothing.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. What's she worried about, what's been going on with you?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the jaw. It clicks, and it aches when I chew. Been about two months. But it's not bad.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): You said about two months. Can you place it any tighter than that?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Work's mad. I'm an accountant, tax season, everyone's shouting. I just clench.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Eish, that sounds heavy. Coming back to the jaw though, when did the ache actually begin?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, I can't say the day. I had a few weeks in my head. Well actually no, more like two months, when the audits kicked off. I just ignored it.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the click there all the time, or mainly with food?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mainly when I chew. Steak's a write-off, I just leave it. Left side, I think. Minor stuff.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): And does stress make it worse?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, deadlines make it tighter. But everyone's stressed. It's not a thing.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does your partner notice anything at night?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): She says I grind my teeth, keeps her up. I don't feel a thing, so maybe she's exaggerating.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or have you felt hot and unwell with this?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The click's louder in the morning, then it eases off. That's all.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Louder in the morning. I did ask about fever though. Have you had one?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever. I'm not ill.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Headaches? Pain in the ear?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No headaches. Ear's fine. People make a fuss.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you taken for it?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Panado. I take four, wait no, two, when it's annoying, which is hardly ever. Chemist also sold me those yellow muscle tablets, can't remember what they're called. Took like three, they made me dozy, so I stopped.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything you take every day? Pressure tablets, that sort of thing?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't do chronic pills. I'm healthy.
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry folks, I still need his obs. I got pulled away earlier.
[SEG0030] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is 36.4, blood pressure 128 over 76, pulse 74. All decent.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks. Let me feel the joint. Open nice and slow, then close.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Click on the left as you open, and the muscle just in front of the ear is sore when I press. No swelling, and you open fully, no problem.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): What I reckon is the little disc in the jaw joint slips when you chew or clench, that's your click, and the muscles are overworking from the grinding. Your body's not fighting an infection, the joint's just overloaded.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): So I can tell her to relax then.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's not dangerous, but it is real. Soft foods for a few weeks, hey, no steak, no biltong, cut everything small. And a mouth guard at night so the teeth stop grinding on each other.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A mouth guard? Like for rugby? Ag, that's over the top for a niggle.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): A thin one from the dentist, just while you sleep. I'll write them a note today. Also skip chewing gum, and when you catch yourself clenching at the desk, just let the jaw hang.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the guard and the soft food haven't sorted it in six weeks, we might do an x-ray of the jaw. I won't book that now.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in six weeks anyway, whether or not, so we know where we stand. Reception will book it on your way out.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks. Fine. And the Panado?
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Panado's fine, two tablets when you need them, don't go over eight tablets in a day. Leave those yellow ones, we don't know what they are.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, sharp. I'll tell her she was half right. Cheers.

spec.situation: Person with jaw pain on chewing and clicking, worse with stress, teeth grinding noticed by partner; no fever; mouth guard and soft diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

bad.reason: Jaw pain with chewing, mild, ~2 months, stress/chewing supported; certainty is wrong—patient minimizes but does not express uncertainty about pain.
bad.text: jaw pain on chewing (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, severity=mild, duration=approximately 2 months, temporality=current, body_site=jaw, aggravating_factors=chewing; stress, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Jaw pain/clicking is on the left side ('Left side, I think').
Steak is particularly difficult because of the jaw problem ('Steak's a write-off, I just leave it').
The unnamed yellow muscle tablets made the patient drowsy/dozy, which is why he stopped them.
